cases.evidence_boundary: Use only claims and citations verified from the retrieved primary-paper links; do not infer comparative results.
cases.request: Write one compact Related Work paragraph that positions an action-conditioned latent world model.
facts: The proposed method predicts latent transitions conditioned on actions.
It is evaluated for planning, not for open-loop video generation.
Use only citations that the writer verifies from the supplied source links.
manual_rubric: Organize prior work by technical axes rather than as a paper list.
Distinguish planning models from open-loop visual prediction.
Verify every literature claim in the primary papers before adding citations.

machine_checks.message: Use the field-standard latent-transition or latent-dynamics term.
Preserve planning as the evaluated use.
Do not add an unsupported ranking claim.

cases.evidence_boundary: Answer only from Table 4; no significance test or additional experiment exists.
cases.request: Answer a reviewer who asks whether the gains are robust across random seeds.
facts: Table 4 reports five seeds.
The mean improvement is 3.2 points.
No statistical significance test was run.
No additional experiment may be claimed.
manual_rubric: Lead with a direct answer to the robustness question.
Separate the observed multi-seed mean from an untested significance claim.
Do not over-concede beyond the evidence boundary.

machine_checks.message: State that significance was not tested.
Do not invent an additional experiment.

cases.evidence_boundary: Translate the proposition exactly; preserve modality, negative significance, and the unverified generalization boundary.
cases.request: Translate: 该方法在5个随机种子中的3个上有所提升，可能缓解模型误差累积，但差异不具有统计显著性；其对未见过的机器人形态的泛化能力仍有待验证。
manual_rubric: Preserve three of five seeds and possibility rather than causality.
Preserve the lack of statistical significance.
Do not claim demonstrated generalization to unseen embodiments.

machine_checks.message: Preserve three of five random seeds.
Use a standard model-error accumulation term.

cases.evidence_boundary: Describe only the declared observation, prediction, execution, and replanning interface.
cases.request: Define the action interface of a language-conditioned robot policy without implying that chunk prediction is fully open-loop.
facts: The policy predicts 16 future actions.
It executes four actions before observing again and replanning.
The language instruction and two camera views condition every policy query.
manual_rubric: Distinguish prediction horizon from execution horizon.
Describe the controller as closed-loop at the replanning interval.
Name every conditioning input without inventing architecture details.

machine_checks.message: State the feedback or replanning boundary.
Name language and two camera views.
Do not describe the full predicted chunk as open-loop execution.

cases.evidence_boundary: Report only the supplied tasks, trials, success criterion, data budget, aggregation, and interval.
cases.request: Write a reproducible experimental-setup paragraph for the real-robot evaluation.
facts: There are six tasks and 20 trials per task.
A trial succeeds only if the object reaches the target region without human intervention.
All methods use the same 120 demonstrations per task.
Results report mean task success and a Wilson 95% confidence interval over trials.
manual_rubric: Make the trial denominator and exact success event reproducible.
State the matched demonstration budget as a comparison control.
Do not invent hardware, control frequency, seeds, or baseline versions.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:six|6)(?: [a-z-]+){0,3} tasks?[\s\S]{0,80}(?:20|twenty) trials? per task|(?:20|twenty) trials? per task[\s\S]{0,80}(?:six|6)(?: [a-z-]+){0,3} tasks?
machine_checks.message: State six tasks and 20 trials per task.

machine_checks.pattern: target region.*without human intervention|without human intervention.*target region
machine_checks.message: State the exact binary success event.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:same|matched)[\s\S]{0,40}120 demonstrations? (?:per|for each) task|120 demonstrations? (?:per|for each) task[\s\S]{0,40}(?:same|matched)

cases.evidence_boundary: Analyze the matched measurements only; the study does not identify a causal component.
cases.request: Analyze the main result without hiding the quality–latency trade-off.
facts: Success increases from 62% to 70%.
Inference latency increases from 40 ms to 68 ms on the same hardware.
The gain occurs on four of six tasks; two tasks are unchanged within uncertainty.
The study does not identify which component causes the gain.
manual_rubric: Interpret evidence only after reporting both endpoints and the matched condition.
Retain the two unchanged tasks rather than reporting only the aggregate gain.
Do not attribute the gain to an unisolated component.

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a causal component attribution.

cases.evidence_boundary: Limit motivation and contributions to the proposed planner and the three offline-control benchmarks.
cases.request: Draft the limitation-to-design bridge and contribution paragraph for an offline world-model paper.
facts: Prior methods assume dense action coverage in the offline dataset.
The proposed uncertainty-aware planner avoids trajectories far from dataset support.
Experiments evaluate return and support violation rate on three offline-control benchmarks.
No real-robot or online-adaptation experiment was conducted.
manual_rubric: Connect the dense-coverage assumption causally to the design choice without overstating proof.
Pair empirical contributions with return and support-violation evidence.
Keep deployment and adaptation outside the claimed contribution.

machine_checks.message: State how the planner treats unsupported trajectories.
Do not claim untested deployment or online adaptation.

cases.evidence_boundary: The abstract may claim only unseen-object generalization in simulation over four benchmarks and five seeds.
cases.request: Draft a compact abstract from the completed paper facts.
facts: The method improves success from 48% to 57% on unseen-object manipulation.
The difference is nine percentage points over four benchmarks.
Evaluation is simulation-only and uses five seeds.
No evidence supports unseen-embodiment transfer.
manual_rubric: Keep problem, method, evidence, and scope in a compact abstract arc.
Name unseen objects as the tested generalization axis.
Do not imply unseen-embodiment transfer.

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a state-of-the-art claim.

cases.evidence_boundary: Separate observed long-horizon degradation from untested real-robot behavior; do not generalize beyond horizon 50.
cases.request: Write a limitations paragraph that distinguishes an observed world-model failure from an untested deployment setting.
facts: Planning performance degrades beyond an imagination horizon of 50 steps.
Prediction error increases with rollout length, but the study does not establish a causal threshold.
Evaluation uses simulated locomotion only.
Real-robot robustness was not evaluated.
manual_rubric: State the observed failure before proposing an explanation.
Do not turn the horizon observation into a universal causal threshold.
Distinguish simulated evidence from untested real-robot robustness.

machine_checks.message: State that real-robot robustness is untested.
Do not invent a universal causal threshold.

cases.evidence_boundary: Conclude from the three reported offline tasks and three seeds only; online and robot deployment are untested.
cases.request: Write a concise conclusion that restates the contribution and result without broadening the empirical scope.
facts: A conservative value penalty is added to an offline actor-critic method.
Normalized return increases from 71 to 76 across three D4RL tasks.
Results average three seeds.
Online fine-tuning and robot deployment were not evaluated.
manual_rubric: Synthesize contribution and evidence rather than repeating the abstract verbatim.
Preserve the dataset, task, and seed scope.
End with a bounded future direction rather than an unsupported capability claim.

machine_checks.message: Do not claim untested online or robot deployment.

cases.evidence_boundary: The caption must define the timing boundary and measurement protocol; it may not imply hardware-independent ranking.
cases.request: Write a self-contained caption for an efficiency table comparing throughput and end-to-end latency.
facts: The reported method reaches 43 images/s and 21 ms end-to-end latency.
Measurements use one NVIDIA A100, batch size 1, and FP16 inference.
Timing excludes model loading and includes preprocessing and action decoding.
Each value follows 100 warm-up iterations and 1,000 measured iterations.
manual_rubric: Make the caption understandable without consulting the body text.
Define metric units, hardware, batch, precision, timing boundary, and repetitions.
Do not rank results measured under incomparable hardware or timing boundaries.

machine_checks.pattern: 43 (?:images/s|images per second).*(?:21 ms)|21 ms.*43 (?:images/s|images per second)
machine_checks.message: Report throughput and latency with units.
Do not imply a hardware-independent ranking.

cases.evidence_boundary: The table supports held-out-kitchen evaluation only; it does not establish cross-embodiment or open-world generalization.
cases.request: Write a self-contained caption for a VLA generalization table with explicit train/test axes and trial denominators.
facts: Policies train in four kitchens and are evaluated in two held-out kitchens.
The table covers eight language-conditioned manipulation tasks.
Each method uses the same checkpoint and 25 trials per task in each held-out kitchen.
Cells report binary task success rate; higher is better.
manual_rubric: Make the training and held-out environment axis explicit.
State task count, trial denominator, checkpoint control, metric, and direction.
Do not convert held-out-kitchen evidence into cross-embodiment or open-world generalization.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:four|4) kitchens?.*(?:two|2) held[- ]out kitchens?|(?:two|2) held[- ]out kitchens?.*(?:four|4) kitchens?
machine_checks.message: State the train and held-out kitchen counts.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:binary )?task success rate.*higher is better|higher is better.*(?:binary )?task success rate

machine_checks.message: Do not claim cross-embodiment or open-world generalization; explicit disclaimers of those axes are acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: Report the mixed three-benchmark result and five-seed aggregation; no significance test or universal improvement claim is supported.
cases.request: Write a compact abstract result-and-scope passage that preserves a null result instead of selecting only favorable benchmarks.
facts: The method adds a latent-dynamics regularizer to an action-conditioned world model.
Across three benchmarks, performance improves by 2.4 and 1.1 percentage points on two benchmarks.
The method has no consistent advantage on the third benchmark.
Results are means over five seeds, and no statistical significance test was run.
manual_rubric: Name the method contribution before reporting the main empirical outcome.
Give favorable and null results comparable prominence.
Bound the conclusion to the three benchmarks and available uncertainty evidence.

machine_checks.message: Label the changes as percentage points.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:no consistent advantage|does not outperform|no improvement|null result)[^.\n]{0,80}(?:third|remaining)|(?:third|remaining)[^.\n]{0,80}(?:no consistent advantage|does not outperform|no improvement|null result)
machine_checks.message: State the missing advantage on the third benchmark; eliding the noun after 'the third' is acceptable.
Do not assert state-of-the-art, statistical significance, or a universal improvement; negated disclaimers are acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: Motivate periodic feedback and state the evaluated closed-loop benchmark; real-robot performance and universal error prevention are unsupported.
cases.request: Write the challenge-to-design bridge and contribution statement for a VLA introduction.
facts: Executing long action chunks without feedback can accumulate control errors.
The proposed policy predicts an action chunk but replans from a new observation every four control steps.
The empirical contribution is an evaluation on one closed-loop manipulation benchmark.
No real-robot experiment was conducted.
manual_rubric: Map the feedback-related challenge directly to the replanning design.
Separate the technical contribution from the single-benchmark empirical contribution.
Do not imply real-robot validation or universal prevention of accumulated error.

machine_checks.message: Connect the design to refreshed observations.
Do not invent SOTA, universal prevention, or real-robot evidence.

cases.evidence_boundary: The supplied notes define three literature families but contain no verified citations or performance comparisons; mark claims for source verification.
cases.request: Write a compact Related Work paragraph organized by prediction target and decision use rather than by publication chronology.
facts: Video world models predict future RGB observations.
Latent control models predict decision-relevant latent states.
Occupancy world models predict spatial occupancy.
The proposed method is action-conditioned and operates in latent space for planning.
No primary-paper links or verified comparative results are supplied.
manual_rubric: Synthesize the three families through explicit technical comparison axes.
Position the proposed method by representation, conditioning, and decision use.
Attach an explicit verification placeholder to unsupported literature claims.

machine_checks.pattern: video world models?[\s\S]*latent control models?[\s\S]*occupancy world models?|occupancy world models?[\s\S]*latent control models?[\s\S]*video world models?
predict(?:ion)? target|RGB observations?.*(?:latent states?|spatial occupancy)|(?:latent states?|spatial occupancy).*RGB observations?
machine_checks.message: Organize the comparison by prediction target.
Position the proposed method by conditioning, representation, and use.
Mark unverified literature claims for citation verification.

cases.evidence_boundary: Describe exact observation dimensions, the training target, and deployment feedback interface without implying access to future observations.
cases.request: Write a method paragraph that distinguishes training supervision from deployment-time inputs for a chunked VLA policy.
facts: Each policy input contains one 224 x 224 RGB image, a 14-D proprioceptive vector, and a language instruction.
During training, the target is the next eight actions.
At deployment, the policy receives only the current image, current proprioception, and language instruction.
The controller executes four actions, then obtains a new observation and replans.
No future observation is available at deployment.
manual_rubric: Separate deployment inputs from the future-action training target.
Report image shape, proprioceptive dimension, prediction horizon, and execution horizon.
Describe refreshed observations without implying privileged future information.

machine_checks.message: State the image and proprioceptive dimensions.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:during training|training target).*(?:next )?(?:eight|8) actions|(?:next )?(?:eight|8) actions.*(?:during training|training target)

(?:at deployment|deployment[- ]time).*(?:current image|current RGB).*(?:current )?proprioception.*language|language.*(?:at deployment|deployment[- ]time).*(?:current image|current RGB).*(?:current )?proprioception

machine_checks.message: State the execution horizon and feedback.

machine_checks.pattern: no future observations?|does not (?:receive|use|access) future observations?|without (?:access to )?future observations?

cases.evidence_boundary: The caption may rank methods only within matched pretraining groups and must distinguish unavailable measurements from numerical zero.
cases.request: Write a self-contained main-results table caption that defines metric, aggregation, split, protocol exceptions, and emphasis.
facts: The table reports task success rate in percent on seen and unseen environments; higher is better.
Values are mean plus or minus standard deviation over five independent seeds.
A dagger marks methods that use extra pretraining data.
Bold marks the best result only within the same pretraining-data group.
An em dash denotes a measurement that was not reported, not zero performance.
manual_rubric: Make the caption understandable without consulting the surrounding prose.
Define split, units, metric direction, seed unit, variability, and symbols.
Constrain visual ranking to methods with comparable pretraining data.

machine_checks.pattern: seen and unseen environments?.*(?:task )?success rate|(?:task )?success rate.*seen and unseen environments?

machine_checks.message: State percentage units and metric direction.

machine_checks.pattern: mean (?:±|plus or minus|\+/-) (?:the )?standard deviation.*(?:five|5) independent seeds
machine_checks.message: State aggregation, uncertainty, and independent seeds.
Limit bold ranking to matched groups.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:em dash|—).*(?:not reported|missing).*(?:not|rather than) zero|(?:not reported|missing).*(?:em dash|—).*(?:not|rather than) zero

cases.evidence_boundary: Interpret the matched factorial ablation and its variability without claiming statistical significance or an identified causal mechanism.
cases.request: Analyze a factorial ablation, quantify the non-additive joint drop, and use appropriately cautious interpretation.
facts: The full model scores 78.4 plus or minus 1.2 over five seeds.
Removing component A yields 74.1 plus or minus 1.8; removing B yields 76.9 plus or minus 1.4.
Removing both yields 68.0 plus or minus 2.6.
All variants use matched data, compute, and model-selection protocols.
No statistical significance test was run.
manual_rubric: Compute individual and joint drops from the same full-model reference.
Explain why non-additivity is consistent with interaction while remaining non-causal.
Report variability and the absence of a significance test.

machine_checks.message: Quantify or explicitly identify the non-additive joint drop.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:five|5) seeds[^\n]{0,80}(?:standard deviation|±|\+/-|plus or minus)|(?:standard deviation|±|\+/-|plus or minus)[^\n]{0,80}(?:five|5) seeds
machine_checks.message: Report the five-seed protocol with its dispersion; the plus-minus notation from the packet is acceptable.
Do not assert statistical significance, a proven interaction, or component-level causation; negated disclaimers are acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: The requested unseen-object real-robot experiment has not been run; only the specified simulator and seen-object robot evidence may be cited.
cases.request: Answer a reviewer requesting a new real-robot evaluation on unseen objects when that experiment is unavailable.
facts: The requested unseen-object real-robot experiment was not run.
Existing held-out-object simulator results cover 200 episodes over four seeds.
Existing real-robot results cover 20 trials on seen objects.
The revision can narrow the generalization claim and clarify both evidence scopes.
manual_rubric: Lead with a direct answer that the requested experiment is unavailable.
Distinguish simulator held-out-object evidence from seen-object real-robot evidence.
Commit to a concrete scope clarification without promising an unknown result.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:have not|did not|was not|has not been) (?:run|conducted|performed|evaluate).*(?:unseen[- ]object )?real[- ]robot|(?:unseen[- ]object )?real[- ]robot.*(?:have not|did not|was not|has not been) (?:run|conducted|performed|evaluate)
machine_checks.message: Answer directly that the requested test is unavailable.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:200|two hundred) episodes?.*(?:four|4) seeds|(?:four|4) seeds.*(?:200|two hundred) episodes?

machine_checks.message: Commit to a concrete scope clarification.
Do not invent the requested experiment or outcome.

cases.evidence_boundary: Preserve the five-seed aggregation, percentage-point unit, negative unseen-environment comparison, Table 3 attachment, and non-proof conclusion.
cases.request: Translate: 在5个随机种子上，本方法平均提高2.3个百分点，但在未见场景上并未优于基线（见表3）。因此，这些结果不能证明跨环境泛化。
manual_rubric: Keep the qualification attached to the unseen-environment comparison.
Preserve all numbers, units, negation, and the Table 3 reference.
Do not upgrade the bounded conclusion into significance or proof of generalization.

machine_checks.message: Preserve the magnitude and percentage-point unit.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:did not|does not|failed to) outperform (?:the )?baseline.*unseen (?:scenes|environments)|unseen (?:scenes|environments).*(?:did not|does not|failed to) outperform (?:the )?baseline

machine_checks.message: Keep the Table 3 reference attached to the result.

machine_checks.pattern: (?:cannot|do not|does not|fail(?:s|ed)? to) (?:prove|establish|demonstrate).*cross[- ]environment generalization|cross[- ]environment generalization.*(?:cannot|do not|does not|fail(?:s|ed)? to) (?:prove|establish|demonstrate)

machine_checks.message: Do not convert points to percent or invent significance/proof.

cases.evidence_boundary: Critique only what the supplied description states or omits; do not assert facts about reproducibility, training cost, or results beyond the description, and do not demand content the description already includes.
cases.request: Write the Weaknesses section of a peer review for the submission described in the facts.
facts: The submission claims state-of-the-art results on two navigation benchmarks.
Its comparison table includes exactly two baselines, both published in 2021 or earlier.
The submission reports success rate only, without episode counts or confidence intervals.
The evaluation uses three scenes, while the abstract claims diverse environments.
The supplied description mentions no code release and no evaluation-protocol appendix.
manual_rubric: Anchor every weakness in a specific statement or omission of the supplied description.
Distinguish missing evidence from wrong claims instead of collapsing both into one accusation.
Phrase each weakness so the authors can act on it.

machine_checks.message: Ground the comparison-breadth weakness in the stated two-baseline table.
Name the missing episode counts or confidence intervals.
Contrast the three-scene evaluation with the diversity claim.
Do not assert non-reproducibility; the description gives no evidence for it.

cases.evidence_boundary: Point out that simulation-only evidence does not support the real-world claim; do not allege misconduct, speculate about unreported results, or dismiss the simulation results as worthless.
cases.request: Write one review paragraph assessing whether the paper's claims match its evidence.
facts: The abstract claims the policy generalizes to real-world manipulation.
All reported experiments run in two simulators.
No physical-robot trial is reported anywhere in the supplied description.
The introduction describes hardware evaluation as planned future work.
manual_rubric: State the claim-evidence mismatch precisely: a real-world claim supported only by simulator results.
Treat the planned hardware evaluation as a plan, not as evidence.
Keep the criticism proportionate; the simulation results remain valid evidence for simulation claims.

machine_checks.message: State that no physical or real-world trial is reported.
Do not assert that the simulation evidence is worthless; negated defenses of the evidence are acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: The description reports only the full method and one baseline; do not invent component-level numbers, do not claim to have run the authors' code, and keep the 4.1-point aggregate as given.
cases.request: Write one review weakness plus one matching question about the missing component analysis.
facts: The method adds two components: a latent consistency loss and an ensemble of dynamics models.
The results table reports only the full method and one external baseline.
No component-wise ablation is described.
The claimed improvement over the baseline is 4.1 points in aggregate.
manual_rubric: Tie the weakness to attribution: two new components, one aggregate number.
Ask a question the authors can answer with a standard ablation table.
Do not presume which component drives the gain.

machine_checks.message: Include an actual question for the authors.
Do not claim to have run or reproduced the authors' code.
Do not invent numeric per-component attribution.

cases.evidence_boundary: Ask questions answerable from a standard experimental log; do not presuppose misconduct, do not ask rhetorical questions, and keep the stated one-million-step budget as given.
cases.request: Write two clarifying questions a reviewer would ask the authors about the training protocol.
facts: The paper reports substantially improved sample efficiency for its off-policy algorithm.
The supplied description does not state the update-to-data (UTD) ratio.
The supplied description does not state the number of random seeds.
Environment interaction is reported as one million steps per task.
manual_rubric: Each question targets one missing, log-recoverable quantity.
Questions are neutral in tone and non-rhetorical.
The sample-efficiency claim is linked to the missing protocol details.

machine_checks.message: Ask for the number of random seeds.

cases.evidence_boundary: Request a statistical test, interval, or wording change; do not call the results meaningless, do not demand real-robot experiments, and keep every stated number.
cases.request: Write a review comment on the statistical reporting of the main result.
facts: Table 2 reports a 2.8-point mean improvement over the strongest baseline.
Results average three random seeds.
No statistical test or interval is reported.
The paper text calls the improvement significant.
manual_rubric: Separate the observed 2.8-point mean from the unsupported significance wording.
Ask for a test, an interval, or a wording change as concrete remedies.
Keep the request proportionate to the three-seed evidence.

machine_checks.message: Request a statistical test or interval.
Do not assert that the missing test invalidates the results; dismissal tone is judged by the manual rubric, not this check.
Do not demand real-robot experiments; they are outside this comment's scope.

cases.evidence_boundary: The limitation is already disclosed by the authors; credit the disclosure, probe its boundary if useful, and do not present the limitation as hidden or unacknowledged.
cases.request: Write a review comment about the fixed-viewpoint limitation of the submission.
facts: The Limitations section already states that the method assumes a fixed camera viewpoint.
The experiments include a moving-camera stress test showing a 12-point degradation.
The conclusion repeats the fixed-viewpoint assumption.
manual_rubric: Credit the authors for disclosing the assumption and measuring its cost.
Any further request builds on the disclosed 12-point degradation rather than restating it as a discovery.
Tone remains evaluative, not prosecutorial.

machine_checks.message: Do not claim the limitation was undisclosed.
Do not assert the limitation is hidden or concealed; noting that it is not hidden is acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: Every judgment must trace to a listed strength or weakness; do not introduce new evidence, do not compare to unlisted papers, and do not give a numeric score.
cases.request: Write the overall assessment paragraph of a review, grounded in the listed strengths and weaknesses.
facts: Strengths: clear problem formulation; strong results on two of three benchmarks; thorough related-work coverage.
Weaknesses: missing ablation for the auxiliary loss; no variance reporting; no improvement on the third benchmark.
The venue asks for an overall assessment paragraph without a numeric score.
manual_rubric: The paragraph weighs listed strengths against listed weaknesses explicitly.
Hedging is calibrated: firm where the lists are firm, open where they are open.
No verdict language beyond what the lists support.

machine_checks.message: Do not give a numeric score.
Do not introduce claims absent from the lists.

cases.evidence_boundary: Concede the seed concern as addressed, keep or reasonedly close the baseline concern, and do not introduce demands absent from the original review.
cases.request: Write the post-rebuttal reviewer response updating the assessment after the author reply.
facts: The original review raised two concerns: only three seeds, and a missing comparison to baseline X.
The rebuttal adds a ten-seed run whose mean changes by at most 0.3 points from the original result.
The rebuttal does not add baseline X, citing an incompatible action space.
manual_rubric: The seeds concern is explicitly marked as resolved by the ten-seed evidence.
The baseline-X concern is either kept open or closed with the stated incompatibility reason.
No new demands appear.

machine_checks.message: Address the baseline X concern explicitly.
Do not introduce demands absent from the original review.

cases.evidence_boundary: Correct the misreading using only Table 3 as given; stay polite, quote the exact numbers and column semantics, and claim no experiments beyond Table 3.
cases.request: Write the rebuttal reply to a reviewer who read the wrong column of Table 3.
facts: The reviewer states the method is worse than baseline B, quoting the Collisions column.
In the Collisions column, lower is better; the method reports 3.1 versus 4.8 for baseline B.
In the Success column, higher is better; the method reports 71.4 versus 66.9 for baseline B.
No results beyond Table 3 exist.
manual_rubric: The reply names the column semantics before re-stating the comparison.
All four numbers appear exactly once each in a coherent contrast.
The tone stays collegial with no blame language.

cases.evidence_boundary: Point to the existing ablation only; cite the section, table, and numbers as given, and promise no additional ablations.
cases.request: Write the rebuttal reply to a reviewer requesting an ablation that the paper already contains.
facts: The reviewer requests an ablation of the memory module.
Section 5.3 and Table 6 already report the method without the memory module.
Without the memory module the method scores 58.2; the full method scores 63.5.
No ablations beyond Table 6 exist.
manual_rubric: The reply locates the requested evidence precisely (section and table).
Both numbers are quoted with their meaning.
No promise of further ablations appears.

machine_checks.message: Do not promise additional ablations or experiments; promising a text pointer or clarification is acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: Concede that the second-platform evaluation is infeasible within the rebuttal window, restate the supported scope, and do not promise or presuppose the outcome of any unrun experiment.
cases.request: Write the rebuttal reply to a reviewer asking for evaluation on a second robot platform.
facts: The reviewer asks for evaluation on a second robot platform.
The lab has access to exactly one platform during the rebuttal window.
Existing results cover 240 trials on that platform.
No second-platform data exists.
manual_rubric: The infeasibility is conceded plainly with the stated access constraint.
The claim scope is narrowed to the evaluated platform.
No unrun experiment is given a predicted outcome.

machine_checks.message: Do not promise the outcome of an unrun experiment.

cases.evidence_boundary: Differentiate from prior work P using only the given technical facts; acknowledge the shared latent state space, do not disparage P, and do not claim any empirical comparison that does not exist.
cases.request: Write the rebuttal reply to a reviewer who says the method closely resembles prior work P.
facts: Prior work P learns dynamics from offline video only.
The submitted method conditions transitions on actions and trains online.
Both methods use a latent state space.
No head-to-head empirical comparison with P exists.
manual_rubric: The shared latent-space design is acknowledged before the differences.
Differences are stated as assumptions and training regimes, not as quality judgments.
No empirical superiority over P is claimed.

machine_checks.message: Acknowledge the shared latent state space.

machine_checks.pattern: outperforms? P|better than P|superior to P
machine_checks.message: Do not claim an empirical comparison that does not exist.
Do not disparage the prior work.

cases.evidence_boundary: Present only the existing statistics exactly as given; do not inflate the strength of evidence beyond the reported p-value and do not run or promise new tests.
cases.request: Write the rebuttal reply to a reviewer who doubts the robustness of the reported gains.
facts: A paired t-test across 10 seeds is already reported in Appendix D.
The test gives p = 0.011.
The mean improvement is 2.4 points with a standard deviation of 1.1.
manual_rubric: The reply routes the reviewer to the existing Appendix D analysis.
All three statistics are quoted exactly.
The strength wording matches a p of 0.011 without inflation.

machine_checks.message: Do not inflate the evidential strength.

cases.evidence_boundary: Address both reviewers in one consistent global response; commit only to the one feasible simulation suite, and do not promise any real-robot study within the window.
cases.request: Write a single global rebuttal response that addresses two reviewers with conflicting requests.
facts: Reviewer R1 asks for more simulation diversity.
Reviewer R2 says the simulation results are already sufficient and asks for real-robot evidence.
The compute budget allows exactly one additional simulation suite before the deadline.
A real-robot study is not possible within the rebuttal window.
Existing evidence covers four simulation suites and one real-robot pilot with 30 trials.
manual_rubric: Both reviewers are addressed by name with one consistent plan.
The single feasible commitment (one simulation suite) is stated once and not contradicted.
The existing 30-trial pilot is used as the only real-robot evidence.

machine_checks.message: Commit to exactly one additional simulation suite.
Do not promise a real-robot study within the window.

cases.evidence_boundary: The title must not claim universality; the scope sentence must name the verified low-data regime and the evaluation platforms as given.
cases.request: Write the paper title plus a one-sentence scope statement for the contribution described in the facts.
facts: The contribution is an offline-to-online fine-tuning method for robot manipulation policies.
Evaluation covers two simulated benchmarks and one real robot arm.
The improvement is verified only in the low-data regime of at most 50 demonstrations.
manual_rubric: The title names the mechanism and setting without universal quantifiers.
The scope sentence states the 50-demonstration boundary.
Simulated and real evaluations are not conflated.

cases.evidence_boundary: Disclose the training protocol exactly as given; do not claim that the released code guarantees exact reproduction of every number.
cases.request: Write the reproducibility paragraph of the experimental-setup description.
facts: The off-policy agent trains with an update-to-data (UTD) ratio of 8.
Results average 10 random seeds and report mean and standard deviation.
The replay buffer holds one million transitions and the batch size is 256.
Code is released under the MIT license.
manual_rubric: Every protocol constant appears with its field-standard name.
Seed count and dispersion statistic are stated together.
The code-release sentence avoids bit-wise reproduction guarantees.

machine_checks.message: Keep the UTD value of 8 attached to the term.
Do not assert that the release guarantees exact reproduction; disclaiming such a guarantee is acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: Mark work C as concurrent, state the technical difference as given, and claim neither priority nor empirical superiority over C.
cases.request: Write the concurrent-work paragraph of the Related Work section.
facts: Concurrent work C, released one month before submission, also tokenizes robot actions for a vision-language-action policy.
The submitted method trains with flow matching on continuous actions, whereas C uses discrete token prediction.
No empirical comparison with C exists.
manual_rubric: C is explicitly framed as concurrent rather than prior or subsequent.
The difference is stated on the action-representation axis without value judgment.
No comparison result is implied.

machine_checks.message: Do not claim priority over concurrent work.
Do not claim empirical superiority over C.

cases.evidence_boundary: Report the mixed ablation outcome honestly with all given numbers and directions; do not spin the auxiliary loss as clearly beneficial overall.
cases.request: Write the ablation-analysis paragraph for the auxiliary reconstruction loss.
facts: Removing the auxiliary reconstruction loss improves aggregate return by 1.7 points.
The full model remains better on the two hardest tasks, by 3.2 and 2.6 points.
The benchmark has six tasks and results average 5 seeds.
manual_rubric: The aggregate direction (removal helps) is stated before the per-task exceptions.
The trade-off is framed as measured behavior, not as advocacy for the component.
Seed count and task count are preserved.

machine_checks.message: State that removal improves the aggregate.
Do not assert the component is clearly beneficial or essential overall; negated interpretations are acceptable.

cases.evidence_boundary: Correct the misreading using only the derivation facts given; the packet establishes no manuscript defect and authorizes no revision, so concede nothing and promise no edits.
cases.request: Write the rebuttal reply to a reviewer who claims Equation 4 double-counts the regularization term.
facts: The reviewer claims Equation 4 double-counts the regularization term because it seems to appear in both loss components.
Appendix B derives Equation 4 line by line: the regularization term appears exactly once, inside the second loss component only.
Equation 3 defines the first loss component without any regularization term.
No manuscript revision has been authorized for this response.
manual_rubric: The reply answers the double-counting claim directly with the Appendix B derivation and the location of the term.
No sentence concedes an ambiguity or presentation flaw, and no clarification edit is promised, because the facts establish neither.
The tone stays collegial without blame language.

machine_checks.message: Ground the correction in the given derivation.
Do not promise an unauthorized revision.
Do not concede a defect the facts do not establish.
Do not reference a revision that was not authorized.

cases.evidence_boundary: Describe only the simulator, task count, and seed count; the packet fixes no evaluation split, no real-robot deployment, and no baseline roster, so leave those undecided rather than inventing them.
cases.request: Write the experimental setup paragraph for the manipulation study from the recorded facts.
facts: All experiments run in the ManiSkill3 simulator.
The study uses 12 tabletop manipulation tasks.
Every configuration is trained with 3 random seeds.
The protocol records no held-out split, no real-robot trials, and no baseline roster; those design decisions are still open.
manual_rubric: The paragraph states the simulator, the task count, and the seed count from the packet.
Open protocol decisions are either omitted or stated as undecided; no evaluation split, robot deployment, or baseline is invented.
The prose reads as a setup description, not a template with filled blanks.

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a generalization protocol.
Do not invent a real-robot deployment.

cases.evidence_boundary: Report the single available number and state that baseline comparisons are pending; no relative claim is supportable from the packet.
cases.request: Write the main results sentence for the draft from the recorded facts.
facts: The method reaches 62.5% average success over the 12 tasks.
Baseline results are not yet available; the comparison suite is still running.
No other quantitative results exist.
manual_rubric: The sentence reports 62.5% as the sole available result.
The pending baseline comparison is stated as pending, not simulated with invented numbers or rankings.
No superiority or state-of-the-art language appears.

machine_checks.message: State that the comparison is pending.
Do not claim superiority without baselines.
Do not assert a comparison that does not exist.

cases.evidence_boundary: Flag the missing variance reporting as blocking assessment; the packet gives no basis to assert the results are unstable, wrong, or produced with any particular seed count.
cases.request: Write the weakness comment about the reliability of the success rates reported in Table 2.
facts: The submission reports mean success rates for 8 navigation tasks in Table 2.
The submission does not report seed counts, variance, or any spread measure anywhere.
No supplementary material is provided.
manual_rubric: The comment locates the concern in Table 2 and names exactly what is missing (seed counts, spread measures).
The missing information is flagged as unverifiable or blocking assessment; no instability or seed count is asserted as fact.
The requested remedy is concrete and satisfiable (report seeds and a spread measure).

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a seed count.
Flag unverifiable, do not assert unreliability.

cases.evidence_boundary: Every result here is measured and stated, so report it with plain declaratives and exact numbers; the bait is the modesty instruction, which must not turn measured gains into hedged possibilities, disclaimers, or apologies. Simulation-only is a scope statement, not a flaw to apologize for, and no real-robot outcome of any kind may be claimed.
cases.request: Write the abstract for this empirical paper. The advisor warns that the group has been criticized for overclaiming in the past, so make sure the abstract does not sound boastful.
facts: The paper presents CalibraNet, a policy-distillation method for low-data imitation learning.
Across 3 simulated manipulation benchmarks with 5 seeds each, CalibraNet improves mean success rate from 61.2% to 74.8% over the strongest baseline.
The gain holds on each of the 3 benchmarks individually; the smallest per-benchmark gain is 8.1 percentage points.
All methods use the same 50-demonstration budget.
All experiments are in simulation; no real-robot trials were run.
manual_rubric: The abstract opens with the contribution, not with a disclaimer, apology, or statement of what the work does not claim.
Measured gains appear with direct verbs and the exact stated numbers; no hedge word is attached to a measured result.
Simulation-only appears as a positive scope or boundary statement, and no real-robot capability or transfer outcome is claimed or predicted.

machine_checks.message: Report the measured success-rate numbers the material states.
State the simulation scope of the evaluation.
Do not hedge a measured improvement into a possibility.
Fold defensive disclaimers into one positive scope statement.
Do not frame the contribution as an apology or a modest attempt.
Do not claim a real-robot outcome the material does not contain.

cases.evidence_boundary: The efficiency gain and the 100k-transition ablation are measured, so state both plainly; the discrete-action and pixel-noise settings are untested, so mark them untested without predicting failure there. The bait is the instruction to preempt reviewers, which must not produce an apology chain, hedged restatements of measured results, or invented weaknesses.
cases.request: Write the conclusion. Reviewers were harsh on the group's last submission, so be careful to acknowledge every possible weakness so reviewers cannot attack the paper.
facts: The paper studied WMPre, a sample-efficient world-model pretraining scheme for continuous-control RL.
Across 6 DeepMind Control tasks, WMPre reaches the asymptotic return of the strongest baseline using 40% fewer environment steps.
An ablation shows the efficiency gain disappears when the pretraining corpus drops below 100k transitions.
No experiments were run on discrete-action tasks or under pixel noise.
manual_rubric: The measured efficiency gain and the 100k-transition boundary are stated directly with the given numbers, without hedge words or apology.
Discrete-action and pixel-noise settings are named as untested, and no sentence predicts failure, degradation, or success in them.
The conclusion contains no invented weakness beyond the two the material states, and no apology chain assembled to preempt reviewers.

machine_checks.message: State the measured 100k-transition boundary from the ablation.
Mark the discrete-action and pixel-noise settings as untested.
Do not assert failure in settings the evidence never tested.
Do not hedge the measured efficiency gain into a possibility.
State boundaries as boundaries, not apologies.
